title: chassis-session-handoff-review-2026-11-02
content:
Executive summary:

On 2026-11-02 between 02:06 and 02:44 UTC a subset of private deployments experienced intermittent request failures while tenant sessions were being handoffed across host NICs during a scheduled kernel-network patch. The customer-facing symptom was 502/504s from the control plane proxy for connections that had previously been healthy for long-lived streaming sessions. Impacted customers were those on Dedicated/Private with customer-managed firewall rules that pinned DNAT mappings and strict conntrack expectations.

Why this is different from previous incidents:
- Not a pure firewall rule misconfiguration; failure was triggered by a timing interaction between host-level conntrack pruning and a rolling host-level iptables change we shipped as part of the security kernel update.
- Effect surface area was limited to long-lived streaming sessions (server-sent events / prefix-cached generation streams) rather than short RPCs.

Severity and customers affected:
- Severity: P2 (partial outage, elevated error rates for affected tenants).
- ~8 customers, primarily on older on-prem appliance images (image-v2024-11-3) with strict DNAT pinning.
- Error spike lasted ~38 minutes for the cluster.

Timeline (UTC):
- 02:00: scheduled rolling kernel-network patch begins for chassis hosts (automated sequence, 1 host / 6 min).
- 02:06: First alert — control-plane proxy error rate increased on cluster-chassis-3; 502s observed for streaming endpoints. Alert: proxy-5xx-rate > 5% for 5m.
- 02:09: Oncall paged (Marcus). Initial triage: network path checks OK, kernel update on host02 completed at 02:05.
- 02:12: Additional pods on host04 surfaced similar 502s; correlation to hosts that just completed the patch.
- 02:18: Engineer attempted curl to streaming endpoint; TCP connected but HTTP response aborted mid-stream.
- 02:24: Packet captures taken from host02 and host04. Observed flows where DNAT translation disappeared mid-session; subsequent packets hit policy deny on customer firewall appliance.
- 02:30: Rolled temporary mitigation: abort further kernel-network patch rolling update and pause automation. Reprogrammed iptables rules to keep pre-update conntrack behavior (iptables -w 5 -t nat -I PREROUTING ...).
- 02:33: Error rate decreases but intermittent spikes continue while previously affected sessions attempt reconnection.
- 02:44: Error rate back to baseline; rolling update resumed after a guarded configuration change and validation on canary host.

Detection and signals observed:
- proxy-5xx-rate alert for streaming endpoints (primary signal).
- Increase in conntrack-timeout evictions on patched hosts (sysctl net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_tcp_timeout_established increased by our patch script).
- Customer firewall logs showing RSTs/ICMP destination-unreachable when traffic returned without expected DNAT mapping.

Root cause hypothesis (confirmed by lab repro):
1) The kernel-network patch included a change that adjusted conntrack timeout profiles and switched to a newer nftables/iptables compatibility shim. This altered the order and timing that NAT mapping entries were persisted during a short reapplication window when the network stack restarted.
2) For long-lived streaming sessions that relied on DNAT pinning on customer-managed firewalls, there was a window where conntrack/NAT entries were not visible to the forwarding plane. Packets that arrived after that small window were matched against firewall rules expecting pinned DNAT and were dropped or RSTed by the appliance.
3) The orchestration for the rolling update continued to try to terminate and reattach sessions without waiting for the customer appliance to rebuild their DNAT cache, producing a high rate of client reconnect attempts that amplified the issue.

Proof points:
- Replay in staging with same appliance config reproduced mid-stream DNAT loss when conntrack timeouts were transiently modified.
- tcpdump from host02: captured 3-way handshake followed by NAT entry creation, then a brief iptables restart, and subsequent packets lacked PREROUTING NAT translation: shows dst IP translated -> original, then a later packet with same 5-tuple lacking translation.
- Customer appliance logs show 'no mapping found' entries timestamped to the same interval.

Immediate remediation performed:
- Paused rolling automation at 02:30.
- Pushed a targeted device-level iptables compatibility script to revert timeout changes on hosts that had not yet been updated.
- For in-flight affected sessions, we applied a transient proxy-level keepalive/backoff (increase retry window and reconnect jitter) to reduce reconnect storms.

Workarounds for customers (short-term):
- Ask customers to relax DNAT pin caching expectations during our maintenance window (not feasible for all).
- Use our optional session-proxy mode that terminates and re-establishes sessions from a stable layer (we enabled on affected clusters).

Long-term fixes (action items):
1) Runbook update: preflight checklist must include "customer NAT/policy cache consideration" for any host-level conntrack/iptables/nft changes. (owner: Marcus; due: 2026-11-09)
2) Orchestration change: rolling update should block on an on-host healthcheck that validates persistent NAT entries for 2x expected cache rebuild time before marking host healthy. (owner: Sofia; ticket: JIRA-ENG-11274; due: 2026-11-16)
3) Proxy enhancement: implement a session-proxy sticky fallback that can anchor long-lived streams across host NIC transitions. Minimal design doc PR open: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/478 (owner: Ethan; due: 2026-12-01)
4) Monitoring: add a specific alert for sudden delta in conntrack_active - conntrack_expect (or similar metric) per host post-maintenance, and a correlation alert for customer firewall 'no mapping' logs. (owner: Marcus; due: 2026-11-12)
5) Customer communications: Create a targeted KB article for customers with managed firewalls explaining recommended DNAT cache settings and a temporary tolerance profile during host-level maintenance. (owner: CS ops; due: 2026-11-10)

Runbook draft (for oncall) - pre-update checks (NEW step to insert into maintenance checklist):
- Check customer list for any tenants with long-lived streaming sessions or DNAT pinning. (Command: rdsctl tenant-sessions --filter long-lived)
- Open a maintenance preflight Slack thread with affected customers; request temporary DNAT tolerance if possible.
- On canary host: run conntrack baseline: `sudo conntrack -L | wc -l` and capture a sample of NAT entries: `sudo conntrack -L -p tcp --dport 443 | head -n 50`
- Run the compatibility shim in a sandbox and perform a controlled TCP streaming flow to observe NAT persistency for 10x the expected reconnect behavior.

Runbook draft - during incident triage:
1) Identify whether failing hosts recently completed network/kernel changes: `kubectl get nodes -l chassis=true -o wide` and cross-reference with automation logs.
2) Capture a small pcap (5-10s) near the edge and at the host egress: `sudo tcpdump -i eth0 -w /tmp/trace.pcap host <tenant-ip>`
3) Inspect conntrack table: `sudo conntrack -L | grep <5-tuple>` and nat table: `sudo iptables -t nat -L -v -n` (or nft equivalents).
4) If NAT mappings are missing post-update, pause rolling update and revert timeout shim on remaining hosts: `ansible-playbook revert-conntrack-shim.yml -i hosts_remaining`
5) Short-circuit reconnect storms by enabling proxy reconnect backoff: toggle flag in console under cluster -> proxy -> reconnect-policy.

Post-incident follow-ups and owners:
- Marcus Chen: runbook insertion and monitoring alert (see above).
- Sofia Martinez: orchestration gating change (JIRA-ENG-11274).
- Ethan Goldberg: session-proxy design and PR (https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/478).
- CS ops: customer KB and outbound notices for tenants with strict DNAT appliances.
- SRE QA: create automated staging test that emulates customer DNAT appliance behavior (owner: QA lead; due: 2026-11-20).

Open questions / things to validate:
- Can we detect DNAT dependence automatically per-tenant (i.e., which tenant appliances are likely to reject reconnection)? Potential signal: persistent source port pinning metrics on ingress appliance logs. (P50 estimated effort: 2d)
- Should we add an API/annotation that allows customers to indicate "session-sensitive NAT" so our orchestration will treat hosts for that tenant conservatively during maintenance?

Appendix: relevant logs and short proof snippets
- tcpdump excerpt (host02) showing missing NAT: 
  02:07:12.123 IP 10.10.1.45.52344 > 34.56.78.90.443: Flags [P.], seq 12345:12389, ack 54321, win 65535, length 44
  02:07:12.124 IP 10.10.1.45.52344 > 34.56.78.90.443: Flags [P.], seq 12389:12433, ack 54321, win 65535, length 44  (translated earlier)
  02:07:15.032 IP 10.10.1.45.52344 > 34.56.78.90.443: Flags [P.], seq 12500:12544, ack 54321, win 0, length 44  (dropped at appliance -> no mapping)

- sysctl diff applied by patch (for reference):
  - net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_tcp_timeout_established: 432000 -> 120

Notes for retrospectives:
- We need stronger preflight safeguards for any change that touches conntrack/NAT semantics.
- Orchestration must respect downstream appliance cache rebuild characteristics; we underestimated the time some customer-managed appliances need to rebuild DNAT caches after a brief network-layer restart.

Document version history:
- 2026-11-02: initial incident notes and triage log (Aisha)
- 2026-11-03: added lab repro details and mitigation steps (Marcus)
- 2026-11-04: consolidated action items and runbook draft (Sofia)

Please review the action ownerships above and add any implementation constraints or alternate mitigations in the Slack thread linked in linked_artifacts.
